newsitem.title: UK: Britain's CWS says no plan to float insurance arm.
newsitem.headline: Britain's CWS says no plan to float insurance arm.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) on Thursday denied a newspaper report which suggested it was working on a plan to float or sell its CIS insurance arm for more than 1.0 billion pounds ($1.6 billion).

"There is no foundation to that report at all...it is absolute and utter nonsense," a CWS spokesman told Reuters when asked to comment on the report in London's Evening Standard. Earlier the CWS succeeded in beating off a bitter hostile takeover attempt by entrepreneur Andrew Regan.

The newspaper said CWS was understood to be working on proposals with its advisor SBC Warburg and these discussions had begun before Galileo, the special bidding vehicle set up by Regan, withdrew its bid. But the talks are likely to continue despite the changed situation, the paper added.

Officials at SBC Warburg, the investment banking arm of Swiss Bank Corp, were not immediately available for comment on the report, which said the CWS was considering putting the plan to its members at its annual meeting in May.

The paper said that any flotation or sale of the business would involve distributing cash to thousands of CWS members, giving them as much or more than as they were expected to receive had Regan's proposals gone ahead. His plan to change the CWS to a limited company and then offer to buy it was thwarted by CWS legal action.

The action will continue on Friday when a London court will rule whether an injunction -- granted to the CWS and prohibiting the use of documents obtained by a senior CWS manager, but given to Regan and his advisors -- will be made permanent. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
